title: LM-X: Explainable Vision-Language-Action Modeling via Progress, Event, and Uncertainty Prediction
models: LM-X (~6B): Cosmos-Reason2-2B VLM backbone (layer-16 tokens), 2-layer Transformer RTG expert, 32-layer flow-matching DiT event expert and action expert with heteroscedastic variance head
action_head: flow/diffusion action expert (DiT with flow matching), conditioned on predicted progress (RTG) and event-expert hidden state
methods: interpretable-by-design heads: return-to-go progress (128 ordered bins), event-to-go action chunk to the next annotated semantic event (60 steps), heteroscedastic action-flow variance
pretraining on >20,000 h of real-robot data including >1,000 h of failed rollouts
five-task RoboTwin2.0 component-attribution gate (action-only, single-head, post-hoc heads, full)
signal-level evaluation: within-trajectory Spearman for RTG, ETG MSE, action-error AUPRC, uncertainty-gradient warning lead time at 10% false alarms
question: Can a generalist VLA expose progress, next-event intention and action reliability as native, pretrained outputs that also condition its control, and does this improve performance?
key_findings: Attribution gate (5 RoboTwin tasks): action-only backbone 63.6%, RTG/event/uncertainty-only +5.2 / +0.4 / +1.6 points, heads added only post hoc 72.8%, full joint pretraining 79.6%; event-only training collapsed open-microwave success from 54% to 16%.
RoboTwin2.0 50 randomized-hard tasks (100 trials per task, 50 demos per task): LM-X 74.1% vs GR00T N1.7 55.4%; LM-X trails GR00T by 15 points on beat_block_hammer.

Real world, 7 tasks on 4 embodiments, 20 trials each: LM-X 73.5% vs GR00T N1.7 50.7% and pi0.5 36.4%; tableware organization alone contributes 14 of 28 extra successes (+70 pp); without it +11.7 pp; regression on tape-roll pick-and-place (-10).

Pretraining vs post-training-only on the same architecture: RTG within-trajectory Spearman 0.71 -> 0.91 and MSE 0.100 -> 0.050; next-event ETG MSE 0.884 -> 0.520; action-error AUPRC 0.49 -> 0.59; failure-warning lead time 0.93 s -> 1.54 s at 10% false-alarm rate (Tables 4-6).
Qualitative traces: RTG drops on target switches and ambiguous grasps; variance rises during hesitation and its gradient marks onset of unreliable motion.

evidence.setting: both (RoboTwin2.0 simulation; real AgileX-Aloha, Astribot S1, Tianji-Marvin, Loong S1)
evidence.scale: RoboTwin: 100 trials per task; real: 20 trials per task; gate: 5 tasks; single training run (authors call for repeated seeds)
evidence.statistics: no: no CIs or seeds; authors note repeated seeds and per-task CIs are needed
evidence.baselines: GR00T N1.7, pi0.5 (same downstream data budget), action-only backbone, single-head and post-hoc-head variants

causal_validation: Limited. Heads condition the action expert by construction and the gate ablates them during training, but there is no inference-time intervention on RTG or ETG to test whether the exposed signals actually drive the sampled action; the authors explicitly state that explicitness does not guarantee causal faithfulness.
closed_loop: Yes for task success (closed-loop sim and real rollouts); signal quality is evaluated offline on recorded trajectories; warnings are not used to stop or recover.
limitations_stated: Explicit signals are not shown to be causally faithful; the model may exploit correlates such as hand visibility, camera motion or episode timing.
ETG is bounded by the event annotation vocabulary.
Low variance does not certify correctness; RTG may drop due to occlusion.
Signal metrics do not establish transfer to unseen tasks; counterfactual tests and closed-loop recovery remain future work.
critique: Interpretable-by-design in the weak sense: the 'explanations' are supervised predictions of progress, next event and variance, not insight into what the network computes; they could be accurate yet not causally used, exactly the gap the faithfulness papers (2607.04681, 2603.12717, 2609.30833) show can occur.
A simple test the paper does not run: intervene on predicted RTG or ETG at inference and measure action change (as 2609.30833 does for waypoints).
Large-scale comparisons confound the explanation heads with a different backbone, 20k hours of proprietary data and failure data; only the 5-task gate isolates the heads, and it is a single run.
Real-world gains are dominated by one task, with 20 trials per task and no intervals.
Including failed rollouts in pretraining is a notable data choice that may itself explain gains in progress and failure prediction.
one_line: LM-X is a 6B VLA pretrained on 20,000 hours of real robot data to also output task progress, the action sequence to the next semantic event, and per-action uncertainty, which improves success over GR00T N1.7 and gives usable progress and failure-warning signals, but whether these signals faithfully drive the actions is untested.
